studies.label: Formal user study: Low, Medium, and Intensive control of research-ideation agents

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 13, Section 5.3.1, exclusions and analyzed sample
counts_source.quote: This resulted in 51 valid data points, with 17 for each control level.

arms.name: Low
arms.description: Researchers provide keywords and generate, select, and customize seed ideas; subsequent literature selection, proposal writing, critique, and revision are automated, without steering the Writer or Evaluator (PDF p. 8, Table 3 and Section 3.3.1).

arms.name: Medium
arms.description: Researchers select literature, prompt section-level revisions, customize evaluation criteria, and select agent-suggested improvements; direct text editing, inline revision, and feedback on agent critiques are unavailable (PDF p. 8, Table 3 and Section 3.3.1).

arms.name: Intensive
arms.description: Researchers have the Medium controls plus direct content editing, inline text prompting, feedback on agent critiques, and customization of suggested improvements (PDF p. 8, Table 3 and Section 3.3.1).

studies.country: United States, Jamaica, France, Korea, Canada, Germany, and India in the recruited sample (PDF p. 31, Appendix E, Table 8); locations of retained participants are not separately reported.
studies.task: Researchers generate ideas in their own research area and develop proposals containing literature synthesis, research goals, and a study plan, saving satisfactory drafts and choosing their best draft (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 5.1; PDF p. 29, Appendix C.2).

ai_tool.name: ResearchGuru: GPT-4.1 for Ideator and Writer; Claude Sonnet 3.7 for Evaluator
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 3.3.2 (final system models and Figure 2 caption for ResearchGuru); model release years are not stated.

estimates.notes: Retains full-arm summaries for this configuration comparison. No pairwise difference, SE, confidence interval, test, p-value, or standardized effect is printed. The complete Table 4 row in sources includes the three-arm omnibus ANOVA; that test is not assigned to this pairwise record. Appendix F.1 and Tables 9-10 concern other logged actions, not unique-proposal fluency (PDF pp. 30 and 32). The SDs summarize participant-level hourly counts; se_basis=participant describes the level of these available arm summaries and does not imply a printed pairwise SE. The paper prints the study-wide count and per-arm counts but no total specifically for this pair, so n_total remains null without summing. For ai_design, treatment is the configuration with greater human control. These contrasts share participants. Printed precision, including the Medium SD, is preserved in the source quote.

open_items: The operational rule distinguishing a unique research proposal from a revision is not stated. The printed hourly normalization is retained without conversion to a raw count (PDF pp. 12-14, Sections 5.3.1 and 6.1, Table 4).

Generate_seed_ideas is not defined clearly enough to separate function invocations from individual returned ideas; excluded pending clarification of the logged event (PDF p. 14, Table 4; PDF p. 30, Appendix D).

Actual total and arm-specific counts at random assignment are not separately established; Section 5.2 describes recruitment and target allocation, while Section 5.3.1 gives analyzed counts. All n_randomized fields remain null (PDF pp. 12-13).

No pairwise total sample count, pairwise test, difference, SE, interval, or standardized effect is printed for unique-proposal fluency. Only arm means, SDs, counts, and an omnibus test are available (PDF pp. 13-14; PDF pp. 30 and 32, Appendix F.1 and Tables 9-10).

Task duration differs between the main procedure and the scripted instructions: 35-40 minutes in Section 5.1 versus 30 minutes in Appendix C.2. The implemented duration for every participant is not established (PDF pp. 11-12 and 29).
The release years of the named final-study models are not printed. ai_tool.year is null; data-collection dates are not substituted for model release dates (PDF pp. 10-12).

Overlap between development or usability pilots and the formal sample is not documented, and no reuse of another paper’s sample is stated. shared_sample remains null; pilot participants are not added to the formal analyzed sample (PDF p. 11, Sections 4.1-4.2; PDF p. 12, Section 5.2; PDF p. 27, Appendix B).

S2 and S3 do not state random allocation of people or randomized generation, tool, or presentation order. These model-output benchmarks remain excluded; their initial-draft preferences and ranks do not supply eligible human-assistance estimates. S3 also does not explicitly print the total number of ranked drafts (PDF pp. 27-28, Appendix B and Tables 6-7).

S4 does not establish the analyzed pilot count, randomized condition order, or exact model configuration. The design collaborators are not substituted for an analyzed cohort; the pilot reports no scored creative-output result (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 11, Section 4.2).

The exact interview corpus size after exclusions is not separately stated. Qualitative interview themes are excluded and do not determine the quantitative participant count (PDF p. 13, Sections 5.3.1-5.3.2).
notes:
Reconciled on 2026-10-11 against the local arXiv v1 PDF. Read the extraction specification and codebook first, then the candidate, retrieval, screening, citation, raw-extraction, and difference records. Read the entire markdown conversion in consecutive chunks, including references and Appendices A-F. Extracted every cited PDF page with pymupdf and verified the numbers directly in PDF text. PDF page indices plus one agree with printed page numbers. No effect, difference, standard error, interval, or pairwise participant total was computed. Source quotes retain printed precision.

The comparison file contains only the S1.clusters_per_arm disagreement, resolved below, and no estimates exclusive to either extractor. All S1-O1 contrasts in the screening form are present: Intensive versus Low, Medium versus Low, and Intensive versus Medium. The source slugs differ in wording; records were matched by study, outcome, and treatment/control arms, and A's slugs are retained. The full-document review found no additional eligible outcomes or contrasts. S2-O1, S2-O2, S3-O1, and S4 are accounted for in not_extracted.

Independently checked agreed fields. The analyzed counts come from the explicit statement of 51 valid data points and 17 per control level (PDF p. 13, Section 5.3.1), not from degrees of freedom. Recruitment and target-allocation figures do not establish actual randomization-stage counts (PDF p. 12, Section 5.2). Individual assignment and task completion are explicit in Section 5.1, and the final design is between subjects, so within_person=null (PDF p. 11, Sections 4.2 and 5.1). The study is lab_rct because sessions were supervised via Zoom screen sharing, with recruitment through academic networks (PDF p. 12, Section 5.2). Participants include students and research professionals, supporting population=mixed.

For all retained estimates, Section 6.1 describes proposals participants created, and Table 4 reports unique-proposal counts per hour: construct=fluency, measure=category_count, unit=participant, sd_level=participant, higher_is=more_ideas (PDF pp. 12-14, Sections 5.3.1 and 6.1, Table 4). The task instructions have participants use the assigned AI tool to draft research ideas: outcome_with_ai=true, question=with_ai, outcome_timing=immediate (PDF p. 29, Appendix C.2; PDF p. 11, Section 5.1). These are counts of proposals, not ratings of their novelty or quality. The precise rule separating unique proposals from revisions remains unreported. The hourly normalization is transcribed unchanged despite conflicting task-duration descriptions in the main procedure and Appendix C.2.

Every formal-study arm includes human participation and generative AI. ResearchGuru combines idea generation, literature synthesis, proposal drafting, critique, and revision in a structured notebook interface that explicitly excludes chat; ai_role=other (PDF p. 8, Section 3.3.1; PDF p. 10, Section 3.3.2). The more extensive human-control configuration is treatment for each ai_design comparison. No preregistration or preregistered primary outcome is identified. No reuse of another paper's sample is stated; overlap among development pilots and the formal study remains undocumented (PDF pp. 4, 11-12, and 27).

The analyzed sample excludes extreme post-task survey responses identified using Isolation Forest (PDF p. 13, Section 5.3.1); this post-treatment exclusion rule limits interpretation. There is no no-AI arm, across-person output-diversity measure, or unassisted post-AI creative task. Post-task survey timing does not establish an after_ai output. Self-reports, logged process actions, model-output evaluations, and qualitative or illustrative cases are listed in not_extracted. The three retained contrasts reuse the same study arms and are not independent samples.
